risks.note: Any negative development across the pharmaceutical/API industry can impact the Company's prospects; management states it monitors developments across the geographies it operates in and acts on identified risks.

Manufacturing or quality-control issues could damage the Company's reputation and adversely affect business, results of operations and financial condition; mitigated by GMP-standard facilities and an in-house R&D team performing quality/efficacy checks.

Faces competition from both domestic and international players; the Company relies on economies of scale, two decades of long-term relationships with marquee customers, and R&D aimed at reducing costs and improving turnaround time.

Profitability and margins are directly impacted by volatility in raw-material prices and operational costs; the Company has built relationships with alternative suppliers over the years to safeguard its supply chain.
Revenues are spread across various currencies, so drastic fluctuations could affect overall revenue; mitigated through hedging strategies and frameworks.

risks.risk: Pricing pressure and global supply-chain reliance
risks.note: The industry faces structural pricing pressure, particularly in generics, and continued reliance on complex global supply chains, both of which can compress margins and disrupt operations.

Regulatory risks and compliance requirements can significantly impact operations, while high research failure rates remain an inherent challenge in drug development, creating uncertainty around commercialization outcomes.

growth verticals / optionality: CDMO with global innovators (2 active discussions); US branded generics via Stellon; CAR-T cell therapy (12-15mo R&D phase); emerging market injectables post-WHO-GMP; non-immunosuppressant API expansion (Nystatin, oncology)

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.

hero.oneLiner: Concord Biotech is an R&D-driven biopharmaceutical company manufacturing Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) via fermentation and semi-synthetic processes, and finished formulations, distributed across 70+ countries.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Concord Biotech is an R&D-driven biopharmaceutical company manufacturing Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) via fermentation and semi-synthetic processes, and finished formulations, distributed across 70+ countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Concord Biotech researches, develops, manufactures and sells Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (through fermentation and semi-synthetic processes) and finished formulations, spanning immunosuppressants, oncology, anti-infectives, nephrology and critical care. It also runs a Contract Research & Manufacturing Services (CDMO) vertical for global biopharmaceutical companies, undertaking strain improvement, media/process optimization and scale-up from R&D to commercial production. The Company serves over 300 customers across more than 70 countries with established distribution in the USA, Europe, Japan, Latin America, Africa, Asia and India.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Concord Lifegen Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%), incorporated 21/07/2025 to strengthen marketing, sales, distribution, regulatory compliance, logistics and customer support across domestic and international markets; also a related party under lease and sale-of-goods contracts.
- Stellon Biotech Inc. — subsidiary: US-incorporated subsidiary (75% equity stake), acquired 01/07/2025, intended as a dedicated platform for marketing, distribution and sale of Concord's products in the US market.
- Concord Biotech Japan KK — JV: Joint venture (50% held), associated since 23-10-2019; also a related party under a Sale of Goods contract (2024-2029).
- Clean Max Everglades Private Limited — associate: Associate (26% held), incorporated solely to supply renewable energy to the Company; Concord has no representation on its board and no entitlement to its profits/net worth, holding the stake only to satisfy captive-status requirements under the Electricity Act; not consolidated.
- Mrs. Manju Vaid — related party: Wife of Chairman & Managing Director; counterparty to a lease agreement for the Corporate Office.
- Col. S.K. Vaid — related party: Brother of the Managing Director; provides professional services to the Company under a service contract.
- Ravi Kapoor & Associates — related party: Firm in which Director Mr. Ravi Kapoor is a partner; provides professional services to the Company under a service contract.
- Mrs. Megha Vaid — related party: Wife of the Joint Managing Director; receives Board-reviewed remuneration.
- Mrs. Sonal Kumra — related party: Daughter of the Managing Director; receives Board-reviewed remuneration.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: CDMO with global innovators (2 active discussions); US branded generics via Stellon; CAR-T cell therapy (12-15mo R&D phase); emerging market injectables post-WHO-GMP; non-immunosuppressant API expansion (Nystatin, oncology)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Biopharmaceutical innovation and rising demand for biologics and gene therapies are reshaping API development pipelines toward high-value, complex APIs
- Sustainability and green/continuous manufacturing adoption are becoming integral to operational strategy and regulatory compliance
- China-plus-one sourcing shift and the US Bio-Secure Act are amplifying international demand for India-origin APIs and formulations
- USFDA approval for Teriflunomide Tablets received in FY26 opens entry into an estimated US$908 million global market
- The injectable vertical (Valthera facility, WHO-GMP certified in FY26) is expected to become a material contributor to revenue and profitability from FY27 onwards as it ramps to commercial capacity
- FY26 was impacted by US tariff-related uncertainty, geopolitical disruptions, delayed regulatory written confirmations, and deferred procurement by certain Middle East customers, all described by management as timing-related/transition-led rather than structural
- Global API market growth driven by demand for biologics, oncology drugs and generics, with continued outsourcing to CDMOs amid supply-chain diversification away from China
- Immunosuppressant APIs continue to anchor the portfolio on strong global demand from organ transplantation and autoimmune disease management
- More than 10 products under development with planned commercialization over the next five to seven years
- Pipeline of additional regulated-market filings in the US following the Teriflunomide Tablets USFDA approval

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin 36% reported, 41% adjusted; injectables facility start-up costs impacted H1 margins by ~500 bps; raw material backward integration supports cost stability; pricing stable with legacy customers; new volumes may see case-by-case pricing

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: prioritizing organic growth via facility ramp-up; investment in Stellon (US commercialization), Concord Lifegen (domestic sales), and Cellimmune (CAR-T); no dividend or buyback mentioned; debt-funded capex likely for future expansions

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Valthera injectable manufacturing facility, commissioned in FY25, received WHO-GMP certification during FY26 and completed a NAFDAC inspection for its Oral Solid Dosage (OSD) operations, giving it a stated peak revenue potential of ₹600 crore; it is expected to become a material contributor to revenue and profitability from FY27 onwards as it ramps to commercial capacity, broadening Concord into a fully integrated player spanning API manufacturing, oral formulations and injectable formulations. During FY26 the Dholka and Limbasi manufacturing facilities each obtained EU-GMP certification, expanding the Company's ability to serve European Union and other highly regulated markets. Concord describes an overall formulation manufacturing capacity of 802 Mn units and fermentation capacity of approximately 1,250 m3 across two advanced API facilities, alongside 5 approved ANDAs for products from its facilities. Management characterises FY25-FY26 as years of investment in capacity, capabilities, regulatory filings and commercial infrastructure intended to support stronger performance as market conditions normalise.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: confident and reassuring; attributes Q2 weakness to temporary timing issues; emphasizes regulatory wins, facility ramp-up, and long-term 25% CAGR potential; acknowledges uncertainty but projects strong H2 recovery

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Two-decade-plus fermentation expertise and process chemistry expertise underpinning leadership in fermentation-based immunosuppressant APIs
- Long-standing customer relationships across regulated markets, built over more than two decades
- Global distribution network across 70+ countries serving over 300 customers, with domestic B2B/B2C reach via government and corporate hospitals
- R&D initiatives focused on reducing costs, improving efficiency and turnaround time to counter competition
- Relationships with alternative raw-material suppliers built over the years to safeguard supply chain
- Robust hedging strategies and frameworks to manage currency fluctuation exposure across export markets
- Precision fermentation platform generating a pipeline of complex, high-value molecules
- USFDA approval received in FY26 for Teriflunomide Tablets, providing entry into an estimated US$908 million global market

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: CDSCO approval delays recurring; US tariff policy volatility; CDMO deal closure timing; CAR-T R&D failure; EU customer attrition risk (mitigated by long-term relationships); supply chain disruption in fermentation inputs

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Stellon Biotech (US subsidiary) enables direct commercialization and margin expansion beyond API sales; CAR-T investment is a 5-7 year horizon play with potential to position Concord as a global biotech partner, not just an API supplier; 76% revenue from immunosuppressants masks strategic shift to non-immuno APIs like Nystatin and oncology

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen the API portfolio through advanced precision fermentation and complex formulation capabilities, with forward integration into both Oral Solid Dosage and Injectables
- Expand the injectable platform (Valthera facility) to transform Concord into a fully integrated player spanning API manufacturing, oral formulations and injectable formulations
- Build out US commercial presence and regulatory filings through the Stellon Biotech Inc. subsidiary in response to the Bio-Secure Act / China-plus-one shift
- Grow marketing, sales and distribution capabilities via the new wholly owned subsidiary …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Customer concentration] Top 10 customer concentration has fallen steadily: FY22 47.7%, FY23 44.3%, FY24 42.0%, FY25 37.8%, FY26 37.6%, across a base of 300+ customers in 70+ countries.
- [Approvals] Received USFDA approval for its ANDAs for Mycophenolate Mofetil and Tofacitinib Tablets during the quarter.
- [Margin drag disclosure] The deck states that "EBIDTA margins (excluding impact of Injectable Facility & Expenses related to Stellon Biotech) stood at 37% for Q1FY27", indicating the new injectable facility and Stellon Biotech are currently dilutive to reported margins.
- [R&D spend] R&D spends across 2022-2026 are shown as Rs 23-30 crore per year, at 2.2%-3.6% of sales; the per-year binding of these values is not reliable in extraction (see notes).
